statements.t: We believe the scale of this inventory, combined with our ability to work with operators and capital providers to establish long-term development programs, positions Black Stone well as the industry prepares to meet anticipated growth in natural gas demand.

All comments concerning our expectations for future revenues and operating results are based on our forecasts for our existing operations and do not include the potential impact of any future acquisitions.

Alongside our primary focus on traditional revenue streams from our asset base, we will continue to explore the relevance of our assets in energy transition, including opportunities in renewable energy and carbon sequestration.

In November 2025, we entered into a 220,000 gross acre development agreement with an affiliate of Caturus Energy, LLC ("Caturus") covering acreage primarily in Angelina, Cherokee, Houston, and Nacogdoches counties in Texas, which aims to push the Shelby Trough westward toward the Western Haynesville.

To manage the variability in cash flows associated with the projected sale of our oil and natural gas production, we use various derivative instruments, which have recently consisted of fixed-price swap contracts.
Accordingly, we monitor the natural gas storage reports regularly in the evaluation of our business and its outlook.
We also regularly compare projected volumes to actual reported volumes and investigate unexpected variances.
If we have multiple contracts outstanding with a single counterparty, unless restricted by our agreement, we will net settle the contract payments.

Pursuant to the terms of our Credit Facility, we are allowed to hedge certain percentages of expected future monthly production volumes equal to the lesser of (i) internally forecasted production and (ii) the average of reported production for the most recent three months.

The Credit Facility allows but does not require us to hedge, using swaps and collars with a term of no more than four years, up to 90% of our expected future volumes for the first 24 months, 70% for months 25 through 36, and 50% for months 37 through 48.
As of September 30, 2026, we had hedged a portion of our expected future volumes for the remainder of 2026, 2027, and 2028.

We intend to continuously monitor the production from our assets and the commodity price environment, and will, from time to time, add additional hedges within the percentages described above related to such production.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, general and administrative expenses increased as compared to the same period in 2025, primarily due to higher personnel costs, including $5.2 million of cash compensation and $1.9 million of equity-based compensation, driven by increased headcount and projected outperformance relative to performance targets under our short-term cash incentive plan.

The Board has adopted a policy pursuant to which, at a minimum, distributions will be paid on each common unit for each quarter to the extent we have sufficient cash generated from our operations after establishment of cash reserves, if any, and after we have made the required distributions to the holders of our outstanding preferred units.

However, we do not have a legal or contractual obligation to pay distributions on our common units quarterly or on any other basis, and there is no guarantee that we will pay distributions to our common unitholders in any quarter.
We intend to finance any future acquisitions with cash generated from operations, borrowings from our Credit Facility, and proceeds from any future issuances of equity and debt.

Over the long-term, we intend to finance our working interest capital needs with farmout agreements and internally generated cash flows, although at times we may fund a portion of these expenditures through other financing sources such as borrowings under our Credit Facility.
The program will be funded from our cash on hand or through borrowings under the Credit Facility.
Our commercial strategy includes the continuation of meaningful, targeted mineral and royalty acquisitions to complement our existing positions.

estimates.t: As of September 30, 2026, there have been no significant changes to our critical accounting policies and related estimates previously disclosed in our 2025 Annual Report on Form 10-K.
